newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azerbaijan attacks Russian arms sales to Armenia.
newsitem.headline: Azerbaijan attacks Russian arms sales to Armenia.

text.p: Azerbaijan on Saturday strongly protested against alleged Russian arms supplies to its enemy Armenia and called for an investigation by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

Aman Tuleev, Russian Minister for Cooperation with Countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States, said last week that 84 T-72 tanks and 50 infantry combat vehicles had been transferred from Russia to Armenia from 1994 to 96.

A statement by the Azeri Foreign Ministry on Saturday said the shipments were "a gross violation of the Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) agreement". The agreement limits the amount of heavy conventional weaponry that member countries may station in certain areas.
Armenia on Friday denied having received the weapons at all.

Christian Armenia and Moslem Azerbaijan have been embroiled in a nine-year conflict over the disputed region of Nagorno-Karabakh, which is populated by ethnic Armenians but surrounded by Azeri territory.
War over the issue killed more than 15,000 people before a ceasefire was declared in 1994 after massive Armenian territorial gains.
Talks to resolve the issue, in which Russia and the OSCE have taken a mediating role, are deadlocked and the prospects for a settlement seem remote.
The Azeri statement said the alleged arms shipments "dealt a blow to the authority of the Russian Federation and to its role as an intermediary in the Armenian-Azeri conflict".

It demanded Russia and the OSCE "carry out an inspection on the territory of Armenia and the territories of Azerbaijan which it has occupied". Twenty percent of Azeri territory is now controlled by Armenian forces.
Tuleev said the shipments had been "in violation of proper procedure and without the permission of the government".

"At the same time a Russian delegation is conducting talks with Azerbaijan on development of bilateral trade and economic relations, behind its back, Armenia gets military hardware from Moscow," he said.

Tuleev said the arms, worth 271 billion roubles ($48 million) had yet to be paid for and called the issue a further hindrance to the process of integration among CIS states. He demanded an investigation by Russia's chief prosecutor.

Azeri officials have regularly accused Russia of aiding Armenia in the conflict. Armenia and Russia have deep historical ties and many Armenians see Russia as a protector against their longtime enemy and neighbour Turkey, which has close cultural and political ties with Azerbaijan.
